responses.topThreeActions:
Over the last almost four years, I am most proud of three actions I have taken in support of DC Statehood. First, I have consistently fought against congressional interference in our local laws, using my vote and my voice to defend the District’s autonomy whenever Congress attempted to override the will of DC residents. Protecting Home Rule is foundational to the broader fight for statehood.

Second, I have used my platform to actively educate leaders and audiences outside of DC about why statehood is a matter of civil rights, democracy, and racial equity. Whether in national forums, meetings with stakeholders, or public commentary, I have made clear that taxation without representation is unacceptable in 2026.

Third, I have publicly and unequivocally endorsed DC Statehood as a policy priority, integrating it into my advocacy rather than treating it as symbolic rhetoric. Statehood is not an abstract issue. It is about full voting representation, budget autonomy, and self-determination for our residents, and I will continue advancing that fight both inside and outside the District.
responses.intendedActions: I have and intend to hold the line aggressively against congressional interference, including in the current tax fight. When Congress attempts to overturn or undermine locally enacted revenue measures, I will use every available platform to defend the District’s authority to govern its own budget and tax policy.
responses.congressResponse:
When Congress has attempted to overturn DC laws or interfere with our budget, I have responded immediately and publicly. I have educated residents about what was at stake through town halls, media appearances, and direct communication, making clear how congressional interference harms DC families in real and tangible ways. I have worked with my Council colleagues to pass formal resolutions rejecting interference and affirming our commitment to Home Rule.

I have also lobbied members of Congress, met with federal offices, and partnered with national civil rights and democracy organizations to build opposition to these efforts. When necessary, I have supported exploring legal strategies through the Attorney General. I have refused to normalize interference as routine, and I will continue using my voice and my office to defend DC’s autonomy and advance Statehood.
responses.partners:
In promoting DC Statehood, I intend to continue working closely with our Delegate to Congress, our Shadow Representative and Shadow Senators, and the DC Democratic Party.

I have an active working relationship with our Delegate’s office and have partnered on messaging and advocacy when Congress has attempted to interfere with DC laws or our budget. I have also engaged with our Shadow delegation to amplify statehood education efforts and align local and national advocacy strategies. In addition, I have worked with leaders within the DC Democratic Party to elevate Statehood as a core civil rights and democracy issue in local and national political spaces. These relationships are ongoing and collaborative, and I will continue strengthening them to ensure our push for Statehood is coordinated, visible, and persistent.
responses.voterInvolvement:
I believe Statehood will only be won if DC residents are organized, informed, and mobilized. I have already worked to educate voters about congressional interference and what it means for our budget, our laws, and our rights. Most recently, I led a delegation of nearly 50 Ward 5 neighbors to Capitol Hill to meet directly with Members of Congress and their staff to lobby against harmful congressional action. That kind of direct civic engagement matters. It shows that DC residents are not passive observers. We are active participants in defending our democracy.

Going forward, I will continue hosting town halls, organizing advocacy days, and partnering with civic and community organizations to equip residents with the tools to contact Congress, submit testimony, and elevate their voices nationally. Statehood cannot just be a slogan from elected officials. It must be a people powered movement. My role is to educate, convene, and mobilize residents so they are empowered to demand full representation and self determination.
responses.additionalComments:
Now more than ever, DC needs serious, steady leadership in the face of unprecedented congressional interference and political uncertainty. Statehood is not a symbolic issue for me. It is about protecting our budget, our public safety laws, our healthcare programs, and our fundamental right to self governance. Given the level of change and disruption facing the District, we must rely on experienced, proven leaders who understand both the policy and political terrain and who believe deeply in Statehood as a matter of civil rights and democracy.

I have not wavered on this issue. I have fought against congressional overreach, educated audiences inside and outside the District, mobilized residents to advocate on the Hill, and used my platform to center Statehood in the broader national conversation. DC voters deserve representation that is consistent, informed, and unafraid to defend our autonomy. I remain fully committed to that fight.

responses.topThreeActions: I have been a consistent and fierce advocate for full DC Statehood over the years. I’ve met directly with numerous members of Congress and Democratic House leadership, I’ve walked side-by-side with DC residents advocating and educating members of Congress, and I’ve joined public rallies to declare clearly and loudly why DC Statehood is needed now more than ever. I’ve also defended Council-passed laws under threat from the Trump Administration and Congress.
responses.intendedActions: I have consistently and fiercely defended DC Statehood for years. I have worked to develop relationships with members of Congress to help educate them about the importance of DC Statehood and to be our champions. I will also continue to be active in resident actions at the Capitol and elsewhere to join grassroots movements fighting for DC Statehood. And when Home Rule or DC laws are threatened, I won’t stay silent or sit out the fight. As I have demonstrated, I will speak out and show up to declare clearly and loudly why DC Statehood is needed now more than ever.
responses.congressResponse: As a current elected official, I use my position to speak loudly against any and all congressional attempts to overturn DC laws and encourage residents to make their voices heard. I have defended the District’s laws and local control. Not every DC elected official has shown up when it mattered, but I have. Throughout the past 12 months, I’ve worked strategically to push the Council to bring on advocacy capacity, lobby members of Congress, partner with advocacy efforts like Free DC, and use the power of my office to speak in press, public appearances, and directly to my constituents about why action must be taken to defend the District of Columbia.
responses.partners: Free DC, DC Vote, DC Democratic State Committee and Ward 6 Democrats. I am a strong ally and partner with these organizations, promoting their actions and standing in solidarity.
responses.voterInvolvement: As I have before, I will continue to engage, educate, and walk side-by-side with DC voters and residents in the fight for Statehood. These actions cannot be done only when it’s easy or convenient, but elected officials must demonstrate the courage to show up and speak out every day and in every fight.
responses.additionalComments: I try to never miss an opportunity to advocate for DC Statehood. Whether it’s addressing a convention of out-of-town visitors or elected colleagues, or sitting down with our local Scouts or school children, educating and advocating for DC Statehood - and highlighting the inherent injustice that still exists today - must be part of every engagement strategy. It was even my legislation the Council passed to change DC’s license plates to read “End Taxation Without Representation” - to remind everyone that statehood and autonomy will only be won through action, strategy, and organizing.

responses.topThreeActions:
1. I have been an active member of the Free DC movement and other local efforts to defend Home Rule and advance DC Statehood, including public demonstrations, press conferences, lobby days, coalition calls, and organizing meetings.

2. Joined the board of DC Statehood PAC to advance our federal fight for self-determination, directing funds to congressional candidates in support of the Washington DC Admission Act.

3. Been an effective spokesperson to media, helping to shape the local and national narrative in the midst of attacks on DC's Home Rule under both the Biden and Trump administrations.
responses.intendedActions:
1. I will use the full platform of the office to keep DC Statehood at the center of the national conversation by building and maintaining a bipartisan congressional coalition, working with state legislators across the country to pass supportive resolutions, and partnering with civil rights, labor, democracy, and good-government organizations to elevate statehood as a national democracy issue. Statehood must be framed not as a local preference, but as unfinished civil rights work and a critical democratic reform.

2. I will actively monitor and respond to congressional riders and oversight efforts that threaten DC’s autonomy. That means coordinated rapid response with the Mayor, Council, Delegate, and regional allies; direct engagement with appropriators; public testimony; and national media advocacy to raise the political cost of federal interference. Congress should not be able to quietly undermine DC’s locally enacted laws.

3. I will treat every major federal debate, from voting rights to reproductive freedom to criminal justice, as connected to DC’s fight. As long as 700,000 residents lack full representation, our democracy remains incomplete.
responses.congressResponse:
If Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block the District’s budget, I will respond immediately, publicly, and in coordination with every available ally because congressional interference is not just a policy disagreement, it is a denial of democratic self-governance for 700,000 residents.

One specific action I would take is to organize and lead a coordinated federal advocacy push targeting key appropriators and leadership offices the moment a rider or disapproval resolution is introduced. That means direct meetings with members of Congress, mobilizing national civil rights and democracy organizations to apply pressure, and ensuring the issue receives sustained national media attention. Congressional interference often succeeds quietly — I intend to raise the political cost of interference.

I would also work closely with the Mayor, Council, the District’s Delegate to Congress, and my delegation colleagues to present a unified front. When appropriate, I would support litigation strategies to challenge overreach.

Above all, I would make clear that every attempt to override DC law strengthens the moral and political case for Statehood. If Congress insists on governing a city whose residents it does not represent, then it must be prepared to defend that position in full public view.
responses.partners:
Concerned DC Residents and Statehood Advocates: DC residents are the heart of the Statehood movement. As a lifelong Washingtonian, former elected official, and Ward 8 community leader, I have organized alongside neighbors, testified with advocates, and worked in coalition spaces where Statehood has long been a core demand. My relationship with residents and grassroots advocates is not transactional — it’s rooted in shared lived experience. As Senator, I would treat you as essential partners in strategy, mobilization, and movement-building.

National Pro-Democracy Organizations: National pro-democracy and civil rights organizations are essential to framing DC Statehood as a structural democracy issue. In my current role as National Political Director at People For the American Way, I work closely with allied organizations across the country to defend voting rights, civil liberties, and representative government. Those relationships position me to quickly align national messaging, research, grassroots organizing, and federal advocacy efforts around the urgency of Statehood.

Elected Leaders on Capitol Hill and Around the Nation: Building the legislative coalition for Statehood requires sustained engagement with members of Congress and state leaders nationwide. Through my work in national politics and my service as a DC elected official, I have developed relationships with progressive lawmakers, staff, and policy advocates across the country. As Shadow Senator, I would leverage those connections to grow co-sponsors, coordinate public support, and ensure that DC Statehood remains a live and active priority within the broader pro-democracy agenda.
responses.voterInvolvement:
Statehood will not be won solely through congressional maneuvering — it will be won through organized, sustained pressure from DC residents themselves.

1. I will treat the office as an organizing platform, not just an advocacy role. That means hosting regular town halls, ward-based forums, and issue briefings that connect statehood directly to the everyday concerns of residents — housing costs, public safety, reproductive freedom, transportation funding, and protection from federal interference. When people see how lack of representation affects their daily lives, the fight becomes personal and urgent.

2. I will help build and maintain a citywide Statehood coalition that includes civic associations, faith leaders, labor unions, small business owners, students, and neighborhood groups. My goal is to make Statehood visible in every ward — through coordinated days of action, voter education drives, and partnerships with local institutions. We cannot allow Statehood to feel abstract or episodic; it must be woven into the civic culture of the District.

3. I will prioritize youth engagement. Young Washingtonians have often led the moral charge for democracy in this country. By investing in civic education, leadership development, and direct organizing opportunities, we can build the next generation of Statehood advocates who see this as their unfinished work.

4. I will ensure transparency and accountability. Residents deserve regular updates on federal strategy, congressional engagement, and progress. Statehood is a collective effort — and DC voters should feel not like spectators, but like co-authors of the movement that finally secures full representation.
responses.additionalComments:
DC Statehood is not a new position for me, it is the throughline of my public life.

As a student in DC Public Schools, I came to understand early that the decisions shaping my education, my neighborhood, and my future were influenced by members of Congress I could not vote for. That realization didn’t make me cynical. It made me organize. From my earliest days as a youth advocate and student activist, I saw Statehood not as an abstract constitutional debate, but as a question of dignity and equal citizenship.

As an elected member of the DC State Board of Education, I experienced firsthand how vulnerable our local decisions can be to federal interference. And as a national political organizer working to defend democracy across the country, I’ve seen how deeply Americans value representation and self-determination — except, too often, when it comes to the people of their own capital city.

My stance is simple and unwavering: DC deserves full Statehood, full representation, and full control over its budget and laws. Not as a favor. Not as a bargaining chip. But as a matter of fundamental democratic principle.

I am running to be DC’s last Shadow Senator — to help close this chapter in our history and ensure that the next generation of Washingtonians grows up not fighting for equality, but living it.
